steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a library
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to use React and state in your counter app.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Counter component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Counter that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called Counter that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Counter component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named Counter is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The Counter component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Counter component. This is the foundation for your counter app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'Counter' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Counter that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize counter state
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component, use useState to create a state variable named count with an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Call useState(0) and destructure the returned array into count and setCount.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component will have a count state variable initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with 0, and the returned array is destructured into count and setCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the count state with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState correctly. Check that you're destructuring the array into count and setCount, and passing 0 as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to call useState(0) inside the component and destructure the result into count and setCount.

steps.title: Create increment handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component, create a function named handleIncrement that increases the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCount with the current count plus 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component will have a handleIncrement function that updates the count state.
successCriteria: A function named handleIncrement is defined and calls setCount to increase count by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the increment handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named handleIncrement and updates the count state correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleIncrement function is missing or doesn't update the count state properly.

steps.title: Create decrement handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component, create a function named handleDecrement that decreases the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCount with the current count minus 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleDecrement function is defined that correctly decreases the count state.
successCriteria: The handleDecrement function is defined and uses setCount to decrease count by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the decrement handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it correctly decreases the count state by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDecrement function is not properly defined or doesn't decrease the count.

steps.title: Create reset handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleReset that sets the count state back to 0.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCount with 0 as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReset function is added that resets the counter state to 0.
successCriteria: The handleReset function is defined and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the reset handler that will reset the counter to 0.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named handleReset and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleReset that sets the count back to 0 using setCount.

steps.title: Add main container
steps.instruction: In your Counter component, replace the current return statement with a div element that has className 'counter'.
steps.hint:
The div should be the outermost element returned by your component. Use JSX syntax: return
;
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component now returns a div container with className 'counter', which will serve as the main wrapper for the counter UI.
successCriteria: The Counter component returns a div element with className 'counter'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the main container for your counter app. This div will hold all the counter UI elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a div element with exactly className='counter' from your Counter component.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. The Counter component should return a div element with className 'counter' as the main container.

steps.title: Display counter value
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add an h1 element that displays the current count value.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to embed the count state variable inside the h1 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The counter value should be visible in the UI as a heading.
successCriteria: An h1 element is added inside the container that displays the current count value using {count}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The counter value is now displayed in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an h1 element, but make sure it displays the count variable using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding an h1 element inside the container that shows the current count value.

steps.title: Add increment button and wire click
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and wire its onClick event to call the handleIncrement function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with an onClick attribute that references your handleIncrement function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Increment' appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the increment functionality.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Increment' is added
onClick event is wired to handleIncrement function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the increment button with its click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment button is missing or not properly configured.

steps.title: Add decrement and reset buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Add a button with the text 'Decrement' and wire its onClick to the handleDecrement function. Then add another button with the text 'Reset' and wire its onClick to the handleReset function.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the increment button. Use the same onClick pattern you used for the increment button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI now has three buttons: Increment, Decrement, and Reset, each wired to their respective handlers.
successCriteria: Two new buttons are added: one with text 'Decrement' and onClick={handleDecrement}, and another with text 'Reset' and onClick={handleReset}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Decrement and Reset buttons with their click handlers. Your counter app now has all three interactive buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added at least one button, but make sure both the Decrement and Reset buttons are present with their correct onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required buttons are missing or not properly wired. Check that you added both buttons with the correct text and onClick handlers.

lessonTitle: Write a counter app with increment decrement reset
